title: JavaScript — Maps, Sets, and choosing a collection

questions.question: "toString" in { Boris: 39 } is true. Why is that dangerous for a dictionary?
options: toString is inherited from Object.prototype, so it looks like a key.
in always returns true for any string.
Boris is a reserved word.
Numbers cannot be values in objects.
questions.explanation: Plain objects are not safe maps. Use Map, Object.create(null), or Object.hasOwn.

questions.question: When should you pick Map instead of a plain object?
options: The keys are a fixed set of field names like id and status.
The keys are unknown names, non-strings, or you add and delete often.
You only need uniqueness, not values.
You need ordered numeric indexes.
questions.explanation: Records with known fields stay objects. Dynamic dictionaries belong in Map.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: Set is the right tool when you need:
options: uniqueness and membership tests.
key/value pairs with object keys.
a record with name and id fields.
a stack with push and pop only.
questions.explanation: Set stores membership. Map stores pairs. Objects store fixed fields.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: unique([3,1,3,2]) preserving first-seen order is best as:
options: filter with indexOf, which is easy to get wrong on objects.
[...new Set(ids)], which keeps insertion order.
sort then dedupe, which reorders.
an object used as a set with in.
questions.explanation: JS Set iterates in insertion order.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: It stores a mapping and allows any type of keys.

questions.question: m[key] = value on a Map instance (not m.set):
options: stores an entry you can later get with m.get(key).
throws in all engines.
sets a property on the Map object, not a map entry.
converts the Map into a plain object.
questions.explanation: Use set/get/has/delete. Bracket assignment is not the Map API.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: array.map and Map — what is the mix-up?
options: They are the same type; new Map is an array method.
You must import Map from a package; map is built in.
Map is only for numbers; map is only for strings.
array.map transforms a list; Map is a key/value collection.
questions.explanation: The word is overloaded. Do not construct Map to double a list.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: We saw the word map used in the previous chapter for an operation that transforms a data structure by applying a function to its elements.

questions.question: Object keys vs Map keys:
options: Object keys are strings (or symbols); Map keys may be any value.
Both allow object keys compared by identity.
Map keys are always numbers.
Object keys can be objects if you quote them.
questions.explanation: Using an object as an object-key stringifies it to "[object Object]". Map keeps the reference.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Object property names must be strings. If you need a map whose keys can’t easily be converted to strings—such as objects—you cannot use an object as your map.

questions.question: groupAppointments should use Map from providerId to arrays. Why not a plain object?
options: Arrays cannot be object values.
providerId might collide with inherited names or be a non-string.
Map is required by the language to group anything.
Objects cannot hold arrays until ES2024.
questions.explanation: Even numeric ids become strings on objects. Map keeps the key you set and avoids prototype keys.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke

questions.question: Object.create(null) as a dictionary:
options: has no Object.prototype, so in is safer, but keys are still strings.
still has toString on the prototype.
allows object keys like Map.
is the same as new Map().
